family.name: SEO
family.summary: An organic revenue drop after a site migration, with a Google core update as a red herring, a recovery plan, and an agency audit that would make things worse.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What caused the drop?
stages.summary: Diagnose the organic drop and separate the migration from the core update. Think aloud: shows whether they reason from evidence or from the news.

stages.title: The recovery plan
stages.summary: Choose the main fix for the next sprint and estimate the recovery. Think aloud: shows prioritisation under engineering constraints.

stages.title: Three weeks later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their plan. Tests whether they adapt and own the result.

stages.title: Review the agency's audit
stages.summary: Critique an agency audit whose recommendations would block the new category pages from Google. Think aloud.

stages.title: CEO update and redirect ticket (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the CEO update and the engineering ticket for the redirects with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real SEO change
stages.summary: A real SEO change they made or recommended that didn't work. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You've just joined **Petnest**, an online shop for pet food and supplies, as head of SEO. Six weeks ago the site moved to a new platform. Category URLs changed from `/category/...` to `/c/...` (for example `petnest.example/category/dog-food` is now `petnest.example/c/dog-food`). The same week, Google announced a core update.
Organic revenue is down from ₹1,20,00,000 to **₹72,00,000 a month**. The CEO has read about the core update and assumes that is the cause.

brief.caption: Organic sessions a month, four weeks before vs the last four weeks

items: Before the migration, category pages were the landing page for 61% of organic revenue.
Search Console: indexed pages went from 13,000 to 12,704. It reports 351 "Not found (404)" URLs, almost all starting with `/category/`. The old site had 366 category URLs.
The developer says product URLs were redirected during the migration. Nobody is sure about categories.
An SEO tool shows the visibility of your three closest competitors changed by +1% since the core update.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: How do you explain to a non-marketer what SEO actually does?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The CEO asks: **"Is this the Google update, or did we break something?"** What do you think caused the drop, what is your evidence, and what would you check next to be sure?
Refer to specific numbers. The data is on the left.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Map every old category URL to its new one with 301 redirects, this sprint
Roll the URL structure back to /category/
Rewrite category page copy for the core update
Fund a link-building campaign to category pages

prompt.text: Engineering can give you **one sprint** (two weeks). What is the main fix?
Pick one, then explain why, how much of the lost revenue you expect to recover and how fast, and the risk you are accepting.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Map every old category URL to its new one with 301 redirects, this sprint"

prompt.text: Category traffic is back to 84% of where it was. But 41 old categories were merged on the new site, and the developer redirected them all to the home page. Search Console flags them as "soft 404". The CEO asks when you will be fully back.
**What do you do about the merged categories, and what do you tell the CEO?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Roll the URL structure back to /category/"

prompt.text: Engineering now says the rollback will take 3 weeks, not one sprint, and breaks the new filters. Meanwhile Google has started indexing some `/c/` pages. Category traffic has not moved.
**Do you continue the rollback? What do you tell the CEO?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Rewrite category page copy for the core update"

prompt.text: The team rewrote 39 category pages. Category traffic has not moved, and Search Console now reports 379 404s. The CEO asks why nothing has changed.
**What do you tell the CEO, and what do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Fund a link-building campaign to category pages"

prompt.text: The agency built 33 links to category pages for ₹5,00,000. Category traffic has not moved, and some of the links point to old `/category/` URLs that return 404. The CEO asks what the money bought.
**What do you tell the CEO, and what do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: Before you joined, the CEO hired an agency for an audit. Their top recommendations are below and engineering is about to start on them. **Name the three most important problems, most important first, and what you would do instead.**
You do not need to comment on every line.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Crawl budget:** add `Disallow: /c/` to robots.txt so Google stops wasting crawl budget on filter pages.
**Consolidate authority:** set the canonical tag on every category page to the home page (`petnest.example/`).
**Core update recovery:** raise keyword density on category pages to 3%.
**Speed:** compress the hero images on category pages to improve Largest Contentful Paint.
**Redirects:** lower priority. Revisit next quarter once the content work is done.

stages.title: CEO update and redirect ticket (AI allowed)

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write (a) a five-line update to the CEO on the cause and the plan, and (b) an engineering ticket for the category redirects, with acceptance criteria.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about an SEO change you made or recommended that hurt traffic or did not help.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
